newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOREIGN FIRMS' INVESTMENT IN NETHERLANDS DOUBLED.
newsitem.headline: FOREIGN FIRMS' INVESTMENT IN NETHERLANDS DOUBLED.

text.p: Non-Dutch companies invested about two billion guilders in 88 new locations in the Netherlands last year, creating a record number of 3,800 new jobs, the Dutch Economic Affairs Ministry said on Friday.
In 1995, a total of 965 million guilders was invested, which created 3,780 jobs.

The ministry said last year's high foreign investment sum was mainly caused by Arco Chemical Co of the U.S. setting up a new plant in Rotterdam. The final phase of this 10-year project raised the total investment sum for 1996 by about one billion guilders.
Just over half of the 88 foreign investments projects were carried out by U.S. companies, totalling 1.54 billion guilders and creating 2,516 jobs.
Asian firms invested a total of 159 million gulders in 33 projects to create 711 jobs and European groups put 291 million guilders in nine projects to create 564 jobs.
Most investments were made in the computer hardware and software sectors, information technology, chemicals and food sectors.
